content.label: What changed
content.lead: A video that anyone can watch used to arrive as a grey placeholder saying it was not connected. Now it plays.

after.caption: After — the same two videos, on the same page, playing where the course author put them

items: The learner clicks the picture and the video starts.
Nothing is fetched from the video host until they click.
A page holding several videos stays as light as a page holding none.

content.label: How it was checked
content.lead: A real course, brought into a real database, opened in a real browser.

items: A copy of the PA 522 course with a public YouTube video and a public Vimeo video added to one page, brought in end to end.
Three new automatic checks covering what gets stored, plus the 179 that already existed — all passing.
Both videos opened and played in the learner view and in the author view; the institution's tool checked as still a placeholder in both.
One warning in the browser's own log, which I removed rather than leave.

decisions.title: Three hosts on the list: YouTube, Vimeo, Wistia
decisions.why: These play from a plain web address with nothing to register. Anything that needs an account, a licence or an admin cannot be guessed at and keeps the honest placeholder.

decisions.title: Kept the storage shape the course already uses
decisions.why: It is the only shape proven to survive a save-and-reopen in the editor. Inventing a new one to hold a video would have risked losing the video the first time an author edited the page.

decisions.title: The screen decides from the web address, not from a stored flag
decisions.why: Courses brought in before this work only carry the address. Reading that is what lets them improve without being brought in again.

decisions.title: The video loads only when the learner clicks it
decisions.why: A page can hold several videos. Loading them all up front makes the page slow and hands the learner's visit to the video host before they have asked for anything.

decisions.title: Interactive exercises stay placeholders
decisions.why: 12 of the 53 embedded panels in the two real courses are interactive exercises rather than video. They would need their own look and their own decision about how a learner's answers are kept; that is not this piece of work.

decisions.title: No automatic check on the screen half
decisions.why: This part of the product has no automatic screen checking of any kind yet. Adding the first one is a piece of work in its own right, so the screen half was checked by hand and photographed instead.

next.if_nothing: The work sits finished and unshipped. It reaches the shared copy whenever the course-arrival work does, and needs nothing from you to get there.
